quote_text:
Of course, very proud. And I have been proud all  the time with them. Maybe the biggest thing—yes,  
we needed these three points, the situation  where we are—but we were hurting a lot after  
last weekend and people were saying a lot of  things, you know, what kind of team we are.
Yes, I could not be more proud, but I knew it,  that the boys, they will bounce back from this  
last weekend against Hearts. Yeah,  obviously you want an early goal,  
but it's a long time to defend  against a team as good as Celtic.
But you need to take your chances, you know.  Actually, I felt it very, very comfortable  
through the whole match. Of course, it helped  we took our chance, but it felt all the time  
we managed to nullify the threats there. And  there was a lot of good, good, good performances  
starting from our two strikers, how they—without  the ball—how they handled it, the centre-backs  
and the two number six midfielders. Plus, when  we got the ball, there was always threat there.
Our wingers in 4-4-2 shape just followed the  full-backs when they made the deep run. A lot  
of running. The two midfielders took the number  eights out there. We isolated our full-backs  
against very good, skillful wingers—one v  one situations—needed to handle that. Two  
centre-backs were playing against a striker who  is always a threat behind. And then, of course,  
as we know, Andy—he’s world class—saves. And  he has those saves we needed in these matches.
But overall, it was a fun, fun game,  fun experience and good to go there.  
But nothing has changed. We needed these three  points, especially with the results yesterday,  
what we can't do anything about. We  needed to stay in this fight, compete,  
give us a chance, and we did it very much today.
Of course. Of course. Of course. Of course. You  know, and to be fair, no one expected it. But  
we said it during the week: football is crazy.  And we needed that. And you need these unexpected  
things to happen, and it happened today. Overall,  we frustrated them. We frustrated them. They  
pushed everything they had, and yes, you need  the rub of the green—or how you call this—luck,  
as well. But that's normal in these  games. So, very good performance.
Of course. And actually, before the match,  these weeks leading here, you know that it's  
full of Celtic fans, but it felt like it was  our home match. It was our home stadium. Our  
fans—amazing again. One stand, big noise, and they  showed whose stadium it is, who is the home team.
Yes, of course. I've been talking a lot about  the confidence, about what things are happening,  
what's happening there. I said it after the Hibs  match that it should not affect our confidence  
because that's a part of football. That given  day we did not perform. We know we can do better,  
but if you don't perform, you should know. We need  to perform, take care of our performance—we did it  
today. But then again, next week is a new game  against a new opponent, new kind of environment,  
new kind of tactical twist, you know.  So we need to prepare ourselves there.
But I'm happy for my players because  it has not been easy for them.
Yes, of course. And our theme was that we  call fearless. We call fearless because  
people have written us off—especially the  gap when you’re coming here. But that's  
how we always handle the situation here in  the club. We were very frank with ourselves,  
that it can be a possibility that Sunday  when we walk here, McDiarmid Park, 10:30,  
that the gap has grown bigger  depending how the results go.
So it could affect you negatively or put you down.  Nothing to do—our players, they walked in chest  
up. “Okay, this is the situation now, let's go.”  And I think they showed it on the field very much.
It was important that we get the three  points. The morale has—it's attitude.  
Confidence is there. Morale is there. But of  course, I love to see my players smiling. I  
hate to see them when they're suffering, when  they're frustrated. But I love that when they  
are smiling. But most important thing was these  three points. The morale and things are—we believe  
in what we are doing. We believe in what we are  doing. But these three points—most important.
Of course. The fight continues. The fight  continues. We have—how many games do we have  
left? Nothing has changed. Is it easy? No.  Of course, I think we are big favourites to  
go down. But we’ve not, the last three months,  given any thought about that. We go. We do our  
work. Some days, as today, we are so good. I  know we are good. Then we need to do it again.
Yeah. And I think, you know, we have been  talking a lot about our goalkeeper situation,  
and I said it all the time for  a reason. I know it was not fair  
for the keepers we had here before—to start  the pre-season without the goalkeeper coach,  
training by themselves—it did not give  them the good start for the season.
But then, of course, now when Andy has come back,  we can see the facts. The performances, points,  
the calmness, the saves—what he has brought  here. And that was not, you know—it was a big  
backing from the club, because it was not easy  to get him here. And he's a top, top keeper.
Yeah, looked like he twisted his  ankle. So walking with the crutches,  
but that's maybe precaution, you know, to take  the weight off. So we’ll know better tomorrow.
title: ‘We NULLIFIED Celtic’ | Simo Valakari Post Match Interview | St Johnstone 1-0 Celtic
